newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds mixed, spreads tighten.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds mixed, spreads tighten.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were mostly mixed and yield spreads to Treasuries tightened modestly in late trade on Tuesday.
Fixed-coupon pass-through yield spreads were about three basis points tighter to Treasuries earlier in the session as buyers outnumbered sellers, traders said.
"There were buyers of just about everything and no sellers to speak of," said one pass-through trader at firm in New York.
One market player bought about $500 million of Dwarf 7.0s, the trader said.
Fannie Mae mortgage-backeds with underlying 15-year mortgages are referred to as Dwarfs.
"Mortgages had a good day today," another trader said. He could not confirm the buying for Dwarfs, but said pass -throughs and adjustable-rate-mortgages (ARMs) were well bid.
By late afternoon, mortgages prices ranged from 1/32 higher to 3/32 lower. Comparable Treasury paper traded off 4/32.
The Treasury's auction of $17 billion of three-year securities attracted less bidding interest than had been hoped for, weighing down Treasury prices, analysts said.
The Treasury is set to sell $12 billion auction of 10-year issues on Wednesday.
In key mortgage coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was even at 99-15/32, yielding 96 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were up 1/32 at 99-18/32 and Freddie Mac paper was off 1/32 at 99-21/32.
Five-year Treasuries were off 4/32 at 6.56 percent, and 10-year notes were down 4/32 at 6.67 percent.
